description: Change a portal's settings: name, subdomain, locale, theme, colour, sign-in type (the login window). The answer says where the menu is now (`menu`) and whether the change moved it (`menu_moved`), who gets into the portal now (`access`), whether your call changed that (`access_changed`) and whether people can create their own accounts (`self_registration`).

auth_type.description: The portal's sign-in (the login window): 0=public: anyone with the link gets in, no sign-in; 1=one shared login and password for everyone; 2=sign-in required: each person signs in with their own login and password. The numbers are for this call only: never show them to the person. This tool cannot let people register themselves (create their own accounts): the owner switches that in the portal's settings; accounts are otherwise made by inviting people (invite_portal_user).

color.description: The colour: 0=White, 1=Black, 2=Grey, 3=Blue, 4=Green, 5=Orange, 6=Red. In themes 0, 1, 3, 4, 12, 13 0 is a light menu with dark letters, and 1–6 a menu of that colour with white letters. It keeps the theme and the menu's place.

theme.description: The theme, which also decides where the menu is: 0=Standard (menu: a bar across the top), 1=Professional (menu: a narrow strip of icons on the left that opens on hover), 3=Professional Opened (menu: an always-open panel on the left), 4=Wide (menu: a narrow strip of icons on the left that opens on hover), 9=Fullscreen (menu: no menu bar), 11=Carbon dark (menu: a bar across the top), 12=Left list (menu: an always-open panel on the left), 13=Right list (menu: an always-open panel on the right). A theme decides where the menu is, so a theme change can move it. When the person said where the menu must be, that decides the theme: left → 12, right → 13, top → 0 or 11. For colours use `color`: it keeps the theme, so the menu stays where it is.

name: update_portal_settings
